classification.difficultyReason: The student must read the stated similarity BCFE ~ EFDA and see that EF is the long base of the upper trapezium and the short base of the lower one. They then pair BC with EF and EF with AD, set up y/6 = 6/4 and solve. This is a single linear proportion with a one-step solve. The unknown is the larger base, so there is no quadratic or square root, which makes it easier than the same configuration with the middle base unknown (p34-q5). It is harder than the plain triangle correspondences in p32-q2 because one segment plays two roles and no side pairing is shown. It is a routine linked procedure, with no unsignposted insight, and sits just below A4.

content.prompt: Trapezia $BCFE$ and $EFDA$ are similar. Find the value of $y$.

answer.worked:
Corresponding bases are $BC\leftrightarrow EF$ and $EF\leftrightarrow AD$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{y}{6}&=\frac{6}{4}\\y&=\frac{6}{4}\times6\\y&=9\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
